⏺ In DeFi you often interact with a website UI, not the protocol directly
⏺ DNS or UI compromise can trick you into signing malicious actions
⏺ This post explains why front-end risk can be worse than smart contract risk

1️⃣ What Breaks — domains, DNS, CDNs, browser extensions, ad injections.

4️⃣ Basic Defense — bookmark URLs, verify domains, cross-check contract addresses, avoid ad links.
5️⃣ Advanced Defense — hardware wallets, tx simulation, allowlists, separate browser profiles.

Final Thoughts

The chain can be honest while the interface isn’t. In DeFi, the weak point is often the path to your signature.

China’s Yemen Assembly Line

The Houthis no longer need to wait for Iran to deliver a finished missile in a fishing boat. 

China is supplying the parts catalog: dual-use electronics, industrial machines, engines and drone equipment. 

All of that arrive as commercial cargo and can become missiles or attack drones after a short trip through a Yemeni workshop. 

The old supply chain was Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, small boats and weapons shipments headed for Yemen’s coast. 

Much of it was intercepted. The newer model is harder to stop because a CNC machine, a radio transmitter or a drone engine can plausibly be sold as civilian equipment until it lands in Houthi hands. 

U.S. and UN-linked findings cited by reporting say Chinese firms have become the largest source of seized material bound for the group, with Chinese-origin dual-use goods accounting for more than 70% of prohibited or restricted items intercepted from January 2025 through April 2026. 

That turns the Houthi arsenal into an import business. Iran supplies expertise, designs and political cover. 

Chinese exporters supply the parts. Yemen supplies cheap labor and a coastline built for smuggling.
